articles.job_description: Apply now Job no: 596052 Contract type: Fixed Term Appointment Duty Station: Copenhagen Level: P-4 Location: Denmark Categories: Supply Management UNICEF works in over 190 countries and territories to save children’s lives, defend their rights, and help them fulfill their potential, from early childhood through adolescence. At UNICEF, we are committed, passionate, and proud of what we do for as long as we are needed. Promoting the rights of every child is not just a job – it is a calling. UNICEF is a place where careers are built: we offer our staff diverse opportunities for professional and personal development that will help them reinforce a sense of purpose while serving children and communities across the world. We welcome everyone who wants to belong and grow in a diverse and passionate culture, coupled with an attractive compensation and benefits package. Visit our website to learn more about what we do at UNICEF. For every child, the right to a Champion UNICEF Supply Division (SD) works to ensure equitable and inclusive access to essential supplies and services for children and their families, in development, humanitarian and fragile contexts. These supplies are critical to saving lives, supporting children’s health and education, and protecting them from abuse, exploitation, and neglect. As the UN’s largest end to end supply chain entity, UNICEF leverages its global reach, market influence, supply chain expertise and partnerships with governments, civil society, private sector, industry, and other stakeholders to meet children’s needs and protect their rights around the world. SD focuses on three result areas to maximize impact, scale, and effectiveness: strategic procurement; supply preparedness and response in humanitarian and fragile contexts; and supply chain optimization. To facilitate and accelerate progress toward these results, SD employs three change strategies: financing for supply and services, supply chain digitalization and supply chain localization. Develop and maintain a strategic framework for the identification of procurement services projects. Analyse and prioritise Procurement Services activities. Share and engage in the opportunities with UNICEF Regional Offices and Country Offices (RO/CO) through joint training and orientation workshops, visits and correspondence. Initiate new Procurement Services projects jointly with UNICEF HQ and RO/CO and customers, through innovative partnerships at the conceptual stage. Develop a system for progress and results monitoring. Propose corrective action when needed. Develop the communication and advocacy strategies and plans. Co-ordinate and implement the communication plans. This includes all components in the communication mix, such as brochures, infosheets, PowerPoint, Internet, presentation kits, letters (especially promotional) and the customer database. Ensure the development and maintenance of Procurement Services site usability and functionality. Ensure the development of web application of cost estimates. Implement e-procurement in accordance with UNICEF strategy. Take advantage of the internet for strategic communication. If you would like to know more about this position, please review the complete Job Description here: Procurement Services Manager_P4 To qualify as an advocate for every child you will have… Education: Master or equivalent (Advanced University Degree) in Business Administration, Management, and any other related fields. Work Experience: 8 years of progressively responsible professional work experience in marketing or leading customer-service teams or related field with 2-3 years, demonstrated experience in managing large, multi-stakeholder projects. Skills: Analytical, negotiation, and advocacy skills. Excellent communication and presentation skills. Excellent computer skills including internet navigation and publishing applications. Language Requirements: Fluency in English is required. Knowledge of another official UN language (Arabic, Chinese, French, Russian or Spanish) is an asset. Relevant experience at country level, particularly in development, fragile settings and humanitarian contexts. UNICEF's Core Values of Care, Respect, Integrity, Trust and Accountability and Sustainability (CRITAS) underpin everything we do and how we do it. Get acquainted with Our Values Charter: UNICEF Values The UNICEF competencies required for this post are… (2) Demonstrates self-awareness and ethical awareness Familiarize yourself with our competency framework and its different levels. UNICEF promotes and advocates for the protection of the rights of every child, everywhere, in everything it does and is mandated to support the realization of the rights of every child, including those most disadvantaged, and our global workforce must reflect the diversity of those children. The UNICEF family is committed to include everyone, irrespective of their race/ethnicity, disability, gender identity, sexual orientation, religion, nationality, socio-economic background, minority, or any other status. UNICEF encourages applications from all qualified candidates, regardless of gender, nationality, religious or ethnic backgrounds, and from people with disabilities, including neurodivergence. We offer a wide range of benefits to our staff, including paid parental leave, breastfeeding breaks and reasonable accommodation for persons with disabilities. UNICEF provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process. If you require any accommodation, please submit your request through the accessibility email button on the UNICEF Careers webpage (Accessibility | UNICEF). Should you be shortlisted, please get in touch with the recruiter directly to share further details, enabling us to make the necessary arrangements in advance. UNICEF does not hire candidates who are married to children (persons under 18). UNICEF has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the United Nations and UNICEF, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment, abuse of authority, discrimination, fraud, corruption and other forms of serious misconduct. UNICEF is committed to promoting the protection and safeguarding of all children. All selected candidates will undergo rigorous reference, safeguarding and background verification checks. These checks may include verification of academic credentials and employment history, screening against relevant United Nations misconduct databases, and requests for misconduct disclosures from current and former employers, professional associations, other relevant organizations and participating organizations under inter-agency safeguarding initiatives, including the Misconduct Disclosure Scheme (MDS), where applicable. Appointment, selection and continued engagement are subject to the satisfactory completion of all required checks. Selected candidates may be required to provide additional information and consent to enable UNICEF to undertake these checks. Background checks will include the verification of academic credential(s) and employment history. Selected candidates may be required to provide additional information to conduct a background check, and selected candidates with disabilities may be requested to submit supporting documentation in relation to their disability confidentially. UNICEF appointments are subject to medical clearance. Issuance of a visa by the host country of the duty station is required for IP positions and will be facilitated by UNICEF. Appointments are conditional on the selected candidates willingness to comply with current or future vaccination requirements, should UNICEF mandate it for personnel. Failure to comply with such requirements, where applicable and without a duly approved medical exemption from the relevant UN authority, will result in the cancellation of the selection or may lead to other administrative measures, including separation from service. As per Article 101, paragraph 3, of the Charter of the United Nations, the paramount consideration in the employment of the staff is the necessity of securing the highest standards of efficiency, competence, and integrity. UNICEF is committed to fostering an inclusive, representative, and welcoming workforce. For this position, eligible and suitable candidates are encouraged to apply. Government employees who are considered for employment with UNICEF are normally required to resign from their government positions before taking up an assignment with UNICEF. UNICEF reserves the right to withdraw an offer of appointment, without compensation, if a visa or medical clearance is not obtained, or necessary inoculation requirements are not met, within a reasonable period for any reason. UNICEF does not charge a processing fee at any stage of its recruitment, selection, and hiring processes (i.e., application stage, interview stage, validation stage, or appointment and training). UNICEF will not ask for applicants' bank account information. Mobility is a condition of international professional employment with UNICEF and an underlying premise of the international civil service. Humanitarian action is a cross-cutting priority within UNICEF's Strategic Plan. UNICEF is committed to stay and deliver in humanitarian contexts. Therefore, all staff, at all levels across all functional areas, can be called upon to be deployed to support humanitarian response, contributing to both strengthening resilience of communities and capacity of national authorities. All UNICEF positions are advertised, and only shortlisted candidates will be contacted and advance to the next stage of the selection process. An internal candidate performing at the level of the post in the relevant functional area, or an internal/external candidate in the corresponding Talent Group, may be selected, if suitable for the post, without assessment of other candidates. Additional information about working for UNICEF can be found here. Advertised: 01 Oct 2026 Romance Daylight Time Deadline: 31 Oct 2026 Romance Standard Time

UNICEF is a place where careers are built: we offer our staff diverse opportunities for professional and personal development that will help them reinforce a sense of purpose while serving children and communities across the world. We welcome everyone who wants to belong and grow in a diverse and passionate culture, coupled with an attractive compensation and benefits package. Visit our website to learn more about what we do at UNICEF. For every child, the right to a Champion UNICEF Supply Division (SD) works to ensure equitable and inclusive access to essential supplies and services for children and their families, in development, humanitarian and fragile contexts. These supplies are critical to saving lives, supporting children’s health and education, and protecting them from abuse, exploitation, and neglect. As the UN’s largest end to end supply chain entity, UNICEF leverages its global reach, market influence, supply chain expertise and partnerships with governments, civil society, private sector, industry, and other stakeholders to meet children’s needs and protect their rights around the world. SD focuses on three result areas to maximize impact, scale, and effectiveness: strategic procurement; supply preparedness and response in humanitarian and fragile contexts; and supply chain optimization. To facilitate and accelerate progress toward these results, SD employs three change strategies: financing for supply and services, supply chain digitalization and supply chain localization. Develop and maintain a strategic framework for the identification of procurement services projects. Analyse and prioritise Procurement Services activities. Share and engage in the opportunities with UNICEF Regional Offices and Country Offices (RO/CO) through joint training and orientation workshops, visits and correspondence. Initiate new Procurement Services projects jointly with UNICEF HQ and RO/CO and customers, through innovative partnerships at the conceptual stage. Develop a system for progress and results monitoring. Propose corrective action when needed. Develop the communication and advocacy strategies and plans. Co-ordinate and implement the communication plans. This includes all components in the communication mix, such as brochures, infosheets, PowerPoint, Internet, presentation kits, letters (especially promotional) and the customer database. Ensure the development and maintenance of Procurement Services site usability and functionality. Ensure the development of web application of cost estimates. Implement e-procurement in accordance with UNICEF strategy. Take advantage of the internet for strategic communication. If you would like to know more about this position, please review the complete Job Description here: Procurement Services Manager_P4 To qualify as an advocate for every child you will have… Education: Master or equivalent (Advanced University Degree) in Business Administration, Management, and any other related fields. Work Experience: 8 years of progressively responsible professional work experience in marketing or leading customer-service teams or related field with 2-3 years, demonstrated experience in managing large, multi-stakeholder projects. Skills: Analytical, negotiation, and advocacy skills. Excellent communication and presentation skills. Excellent computer skills including internet navigation and publishing applications. Language Requirements: Fluency in English is required. Knowledge of another official UN language (Arabic, Chinese, French, Russian or Spanish) is an asset. Relevant experience at country level, particularly in development, fragile settings and humanitarian contexts. UNICEF's Core Values of Care, Respect, Integrity, Trust and Accountability and Sustainability (CRITAS) underpin everything we do and how we do it. Get acquainted with Our Values Charter: UNICEF Values The UNICEF competencies required for this post are… (2) Demonstrates self-awareness and ethical awareness Familiarize yourself with our competency framework and its different levels. UNICEF promotes and advocates for the protection of the rights of every child, everywhere, in everything it does and is mandated to support the realization of the rights of every child, including those most disadvantaged, and our global workforce must reflect the diversity of those children. The UNICEF family is committed to include everyone, irrespective of their race/ethnicity, disability, gender identity, sexual orientation, religion, nationality, socio-economic background, minority, or any other status. UNICEF encourages applications from all qualified candidates, regardless of gender, nationality, religious or ethnic backgrounds, and from people with disabilities, including neurodivergence. We offer a wide range of benefits to our staff, including paid parental leave, breastfeeding breaks and reasonable accommodation for persons with disabilities. UNICEF provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process. If you require any accommodation, please submit your request through the accessibility email button on the UNICEF Careers webpage (Accessibility | UNICEF). Should you be shortlisted, please get in touch with the recruiter directly to share further details, enabling us to make the necessary arrangements in advance. UNICEF does not hire candidates who are married to children (persons under 18). UNICEF has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the United Nations and UNICEF, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment, abuse of authority, discrimination, fraud, corruption and other forms of serious misconduct. UNICEF is committed to promoting the protection and safeguarding of all children. All selected candidates will undergo rigorous reference, safeguarding and background verification checks. These checks may include verification of academic credentials and employment history, screening against relevant United Nations misconduct databases, and requests for misconduct disclosures from current and former employers, professional associations, other relevant organizations and participating organizations under inter-agency safeguarding initiatives, including the Misconduct Disclosure Scheme (MDS), where applicable. Appointment, selection and continued engagement are subject to the satisfactory completion of all required checks. Selected candidates may be required to provide additional information and consent to enable UNICEF to undertake these checks. Background checks will include the verification of academic credential(s) and employment history. Selected candidates may be required to provide additional information to conduct a background check, and selected candidates with disabilities may be requested to submit supporting documentation in relation to their disability confidentially. UNICEF appointments are subject to medical clearance. Issuance of a visa by the host country of the duty station is required for IP positions and will be facilitated by UNICEF. Appointments are conditional on the selected candidates willingness to comply with current or future vaccination requirements, should UNICEF mandate it for personnel. Failure to comply with such requirements, where applicable and without a duly approved medical exemption from the relevant UN authority, will result in the cancellation of the selection or may lead to other administrative measures, including separation from service. As per Article 101, paragraph 3, of the Charter of the United Nations, the paramount consideration in the employment of the staff is the necessity of securing the highest standards of efficiency, competence, and integrity. UNICEF is committed to fostering an inclusive, representative, and welcoming workforce. For this position, eligible and suitable candidates are encouraged to apply. Government employees who are considered for employment with UNICEF are normally required to resign from their government positions before taking up an assignment with UNICEF. UNICEF reserves the right to withdraw an offer of appointment, without compensation, if a visa or medical clearance is not obtained, or necessary inoculation requirements are not met, within a reasonable period for any reason. UNICEF does not charge a processing fee at any stage of its recruitment, selection, and hiring processes (i.e., application stage, interview stage, validation stage, or appointment and training). UNICEF will not ask for applicants' bank account information. Mobility is a condition of international professional employment with UNICEF and an underlying premise of the international civil service. Humanitarian action is a cross-cutting priority within UNICEF's Strategic Plan. UNICEF is committed to stay and deliver in humanitarian contexts. Therefore, all staff, at all levels across all functional areas, can be called upon to be deployed to support humanitarian response, contributing to both strengthening resilience of communities and capacity of national authorities. All UNICEF positions are advertised, and only shortlisted candidates will be contacted and advance to the next stage of the selection process. An internal candidate performing at the level of the post in the relevant functional area, or an internal/external candidate in the corresponding Talent Group, may be selected, if suitable for the post, without assessment of other candidates. Additional information about working for UNICEF can be found here. Advertised: 01 Oct 2026 Romance Daylight Time Deadline: 31 Oct 2026 Romance Standard Time

articles.job_description: Apply now Job no: 596054 Contract type: Consultant Duty Station: New York Level: Consultancy Location: United States Categories: Adolescent Development UNICEF works in over 190 countries and territories to save children’s lives, defend their rights, and help them fulfill their potential, from early childhood through adolescence. At UNICEF, we are committed, passionate, and proud of what we do for as long as we are needed. Promoting the rights of every child is not just a job – it is a calling. UNICEF is a place where careers are built. We offer our staff diverse opportunities for professional and personal development that will help them reinforce a sense of purpose while serving children and communities across the world. We welcome everyone who wants to belong and grow in a diverse and passionate culture, coupled with an attractive compensation and benefits package. Visit our website to learn more about what we do at UNICEF. Generation Unlimited (GenU) Generation Unlimited is UNICEF's global multi-sector partnership platform to connect every young person to employability skilling, employment and entrepreneurship by 2030. By mobilising public, private and youth partners, GenU supports country-level solutions and global offers that strengthen learning-to-earning pathways, with a focus on equity, inclusion and scale. This assignment is anchored in the UNICEF Youth Livelihoods Strategy (2026-2029). The Strategy positions youth livelihoods as central to breaking intergenerational poverty by ensuring that investments in education, skills, social protection and other services translate into income, resilience and opportunity for young people and their households. It positions UNICEF to act earlier, act systemically and act at scale, with deliberate attention to adolescent girls, young women, young people with disabilities and other marginalised groups. The consultancy will help operationalise the Strategy across Asia by translating it into practical country and regional products. The work will align with the Strategy's three pillars: systems, policies and data; skills and pathways; and entrepreneurship, income and economic inclusion. It will also reflect the joint ESP-GenU technical assistance model, in which ESP provides the policy, systems and diagnostics backbone, while GenU mobilises partnerships, private sector engagement, financing, innovation and opportunity creation. Role Overview: GenU Senior Partnerships and Youth Livelihoods Consultant - Asia The Consultant will provide senior technical programme, partnership and resource mobilisation support over a 4.5-month period, from 15 September 2026 to 31 January 2027, to consolidate GenU's contribution to the Youth Livelihoods Strategy across priority countries in Asia. Building on existing engagement with country offices, regional colleagues, ESP colleagues and GenU teams, the Consultant will prepare document-based products that can be reviewed and certified within the contract period: a strategy alignment note and pipeline tracker, country investment packages, partnership and financing products, a strategic engagement and capacity support package, and a final handover package with an Asia youth livelihoods roadmap for 2027. If you would like to know more about this position, please review the Terms of Reference here: ToR GenU Senior Partnerships and Youth Livelihoods Consultant TMS text.pdf To qualify as an advocate for every child you will have: Education: Master’s degree in international development, business administration, public policy, international relations, law, social policy, education, economics or a related field. • A minimum of 15 years of relevant professional experience in youth programming, youth livelihoods, adolescent and youth development, partnership development, resource mobilisation or related areas, including senior leadership experience with international organisations. • Demonstrated track record in building or leading multi-stakeholder youth platforms, public-private-youth partnerships, or large-scale youth livelihoods, skills, employability or entrepreneurship initiatives. • Demonstrated success in developing investment propositions, partnership strategies, donor proposals or financing narratives for multi-stakeholder or youth-focused initiatives at country, regional or global level. • Proven experience translating strategy into practical country-level products, including country investment packages, roadmaps, governance or platform models, CPD/UNSDCF inputs, partnership pipelines and handover products. • Proven ability to work across public, private, philanthropic, youth, UN and government partners, including coordination with country offices, regional offices and headquarters teams. • Substantive experience in Asia, including familiarity with youth skills, employability, entrepreneurship, gender inclusion, green and digital pathways, blended finance or youth livelihoods systems. • Strong writing, facilitation and senior stakeholder engagement skills, including ability to produce high-quality written products under tight timelines. Fluency in English (written and spoken) is necessary Working knowledge of other UN official languages is an asset. Youth livelihoods strategy, partnership architecture, proposal and pitch development, CPD/UNSDCF integration, private sector engagement, public-private-youth partnership models, blended finance concepts, pipeline management, project management and remote coordination across multiple time zones. Prior experience with UNICEF or Generation Unlimited at country and regional level is an added advantage. UNICEF’s Core Values of Care, Respect, Integrity, Trust and Accountability and Sustainability (CRITAS) underpin everything we do and how we do it. Get acquainted with Our Values Charter: UNICEF Values UNICEF promotes and advocates for the protection of the rights of every child, everywhere, in everything it does and is mandated to support the realization of the rights of every child, including those most disadvantaged, and our global workforce must reflect the diversity of those children. The UNICEF family is committed to include everyone, irrespective of their race/ethnicity, disability, gender identity, sexual orientation, religion, nationality, socio-economic background, minority, or any other status. UNICEF encourages applications from all qualified candidates, regardless of gender, nationality, religious or ethnic backgrounds, and from people with disabilities, including neurodivergence. We offer reasonable accommodation for persons with disabilities. throughout the recruitment process. If you require any accommodation, please submit your request through the accessibility email button on the UNICEF Careers webpage Accessibility UNICEF. Should you be shortlisted, please get in touch with the recruiter directly to share further details, enabling us to make the necessary arrangements in advance. UNICEF does not hire candidates who are married to children (persons under 18). UNICEF has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the United Nations and UNICEF, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment, abuse of authority and discrimination based on gender, nationality, age, race, sexual orientation, religious or ethnic background or disabilities. UNICEF is committed to promote the protection and safeguarding of all children. All selected candidates will, therefore, undergo rigorous reference and background checks, and will be expected to adhere to these standards and principles. Background checks will include the verification of academic credential(s) and employment history. Selected candidates may be required to provide additional information to conduct a background check, and selected candidates with disabilities may be requested to submit supporting documentation in relation to their disability confidentially. Qualified candidates are invited to submit the following documents via the online recruitment portal (Talent Management System): An up-to-date TMS profile and curriculum vitae (CV) A separate financial proposal Financial proposal Consultancy GenU Senior Partnerships - TMS.docx UNICEF does not charge a processing fee at any stage of its recruitment, selection, and hiring processes (i.e., application stage, interview stage, validation stage, or appointment and training). UNICEF will not ask for applicants’ bank account information. All UNICEF positions are advertised, and only shortlisted candidates will be contacted and advance to the next stage of the selection process. Additional information about working for UNICEF can be found here. Advertised: 01 Oct 2026 Eastern Daylight Time Deadline: 07 Oct 2026 Eastern Daylight Time

articles.job_description: Apply now Job no: 596055 Contract type: Temporary Appointment Location: Democratic Republic of Congo Categories: Health UNICEF works in over 190 countries and territories to save children's lives, defend their rights, and help them fulfill their potential, from early childhood through adolescence. At UNICEF, we are committed, passionate, and proud of what we do for as long as we are needed. Promoting the rights of every child is not just a job – it is a calling. UNICEF is a place where careers are built: we offer our staff diverse opportunities for professional and personal development that will help them reinforce a sense of purpose while serving children and communities across the world. We welcome everyone who wants to belong and grow in a diverse and passionate culture, coupled with an attractive compensation and benefits package. Visit our website to learn more about what we do at UNICEF. The Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) is responding to its 17th Ebola Virus Disease (EVD) outbreak, confirmed in May 2026 and affecting Ituri, North Kivu, and South Kivu provinces. The situation remains complex and evolving, with transmission occurring in both community and health-care settings. Response efforts are led by national authorities in a context shaped by health system limitations, logistical constraints, insecurity, displacement, and diverse community perceptions influencing health-seeking behaviors.UNICEF supports the Government through a multi-sectoral approach, focusing on community engagement, surveillance, infection prevention, and the continuity of essential services for vulnerable populations.This context requires strong coordination, adaptability, and cultural sensitivity to support effective and equitable response efforts, particularly for children and at-risk communities. The health system is under considerable strain, with capacities for isolation, rapid diagnosis, and case management sometimes being limited. Challenges related to specimen collection, transportation, and analysis, as well as delays in reporting and validating data, can hinder the timely confirmation of cases and the rapid implementation of control measures. The operational context remains particularly complex, marked by persistent insecurity, population displacement, inter-provincial mobility, and limited humanitarian access in certain areas. These constraints are further compounded by mistrust among some communities toward the health system, the spread of rumors, and delayed recourse to healthcare facilities or reliance on traditional practices. These factors can delay the reporting of alerts, the isolation of suspected cases, and the effective monitoring of contacts. Implementation of Community-Based Surveillance Supervision and Support of Community-Based Personnel Collaboration with SBC/RCCE (Social and Behaviour Change / Risk Communication and Community Engagement) If you would like to know more about this position, please review the complete Job Description here: GVA - ToR Healh (CSB) Officer - NOB - Mutliple DS.docx To qualify as a champion for every child you will have… Education: Bachelor’s degree in Public Health, Medicine, or a related field. Work Experience: At least two (2) years of relevant professional experience in community-based surveillance or public health programs. Skills: Good knowledge of epidemiological surveillance Proficiency in Community-Based Surveillance (CBS) approaches Knowledge of the community context and local dynamics Ability to work effectively with community stakeholders Strong supervision and training skills Competencies in routine and mass vaccination activities Good knowledge of epidemiological surveillance Proficiency in Community-Based Surveillance (CBS) approaches Knowledge of the community context and local dynamics Ability to work effectively with community stakeholders Competencies in routine and mass vaccination activities Language Requirements: Proficiency in French is required. Language: Knowledge of another official UN language (Arabic, Chinese, Russian or Spanish). Intermediate knowledge of English and national languages, particularly Swahili, is considered an asset. Experience in outbreak response (such as Ebola, cholera, or other infectious disease outbreaks) is considered an asset. Relevant experience at country level, particularly in development, fragile settings and humanitarian contexts. UNICEF promotes and advocates for the protection of the rights of every child, everywhere, in everything it does and is mandated to support the realization of the rights of every child, including those most disadvantaged, and our global workforce must reflect the diversity of those children. The UNICEF family is committed to include everyone, irrespective of their race/ethnicity, disability, gender identity, sexual orientation, religion, nationality, socio-economic background, minority, or any other status. UNICEF encourages applications from all qualified candidates, regardless of gender, nationality, religious or ethnic backgrounds, and from people with disabilities, including neurodivergence. We offer a wide range of benefits to our staff, including paid parental leave, breastfeeding breaks and reasonable accommodation for persons with disabilities. UNICEF provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process. If you require any accommodation, please submit your request through the accessibility email button on the UNICEF Careers webpage Accessibility | UNICEF. Should you be shortlisted, please get in touch with the recruiter directly to share further details, enabling us to make the necessary arrangements in advance. UNICEF does not hire candidates who are married to children (persons under 18). UNICEF has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the United Nations and UNICEF, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment, abuse of authority, discrimination, fraud, corruption and other forms of serious misconduct. UNICEF is committed to promoting the protection and safeguarding of all children. All selected candidates will undergo rigorous reference, safeguarding and background verification checks. These checks may include verification of academic credentials and employment history, screening against relevant United Nations misconduct databases, and requests for misconduct disclosures from current and former employers, professional associations, other relevant organizations and participating organizations under inter-agency safeguarding initiatives, including the Misconduct Disclosure Scheme (MDS), where applicable. Appointment, selection and continued engagement are subject to the satisfactory completion of all required checks. Selected candidates may be required to provide additional information and consent to enable UNICEF to undertake these checks. Background checks will include the verification of academic credential(s) and employment history. Selected candidates may be required to provide additional information to conduct a background check, and selected candidates with disabilities may be requested to submit supporting documentation in relation to their disability confidentially. UNICEF appointments are subject to medical clearance. Issuance of a visa by the host country of the duty station is required for IP positions and will be facilitated by UNICEF. Appointments are conditional on the selected candidates willingness to comply with current or future vaccination requirements, should UNICEF mandate it for personnel. Failure to comply with such requirements, where applicable and without a duly approved medical exemption from the relevant UN authority, will result in the cancellation of the selection or may lead to other administrative measures, including separation from service. As per Article 101, paragraph 3, of the Charter of the United Nations, the paramount consideration in the employment of the staff is the necessity of securing the highest standards of efficiency, competence, and integrity. This position has been assessed as an elevated risk role for Child Safeguarding purposes as it is either a role with direct contact with children, a role that works directly with identifiable children’s data, a safeguarding response role, or an assessed risk role. Additional vetting and assessment for elevated risk roles in child safeguarding (potentially including additional criminal background checks) apply. UNICEF is committed to fostering an inclusive, representative, and welcoming workforce. For this position, eligible and suitable female candidates are encouraged to apply. Government employees who are considered for employment with UNICEF are normally required to resign from their government positions before taking up an assignment with UNICEF. UNICEF reserves the right to withdraw an offer of appointment, without compensation, if a visa or medical clearance is not obtained, or necessary inoculation requirements are not met, within a reasonable period for any reason. UNICEF does not charge a processing fee at any stage of its recruitment, selection, and hiring processes (i.e., application stage, interview stage, validation stage, or appointment and training). UNICEF will not ask for applicants' bank account information. UNICEF staff members holding fixed-term, continuing, or permanent appointments who are considered to be on abolished post status may apply for this temporary position and, if selected with a start date before 31 December 2025, may take it up as a temporary assignment, in line with UNICEF guidance on separation due to the abolition of posts or staff reduction. They will retain their fixed-term entitlements but will not hold a lien to their abolished post. For other scenarios where a Temporary Assignment may be possible, please refer to Additional guidance on IP to IP temporary assignments after completion of the full TOD.pdf (accessible to UNICEF personnel only). The conditions of a temporary assignment, including relocation entitlements, will depend on the status of the staff member's original appointment and may be limited in accordance with applicable UNICEF policies, procedures, and practices in force. Mobility is a condition of international professional employment with UNICEF and an underlying premise of the international civil service. Humanitarian action is a cross-cutting priority within UNICEF's Strategic Plan. UNICEF is committed to stay and deliver in humanitarian contexts. Therefore, all staff, at all levels across all functional areas, can be called upon to be deployed to support humanitarian response, contributing to both strengthening resilience of communities and capacity of national authorities. Eligible staff members on fixed-term, continuing or permanent contracts applying to IP TA positions in a duty station designated as L2/L3, may be able to retain a lien and their fixed-term entitlements, subject to approval by their Head of Office. The conditions of the temporary assignment will vary depending on the status of their post and relocation entitlements may be limited as per the relevant policies. All UNICEF positions are advertised, and only shortlisted candidates will be contacted and advance to the next stage of the selection process. An internal candidate performing at the level of the post in the relevant functional area, or an internal/external candidate in the corresponding Talent Group, may be selected, if suitable for the post, without assessment of other candidates. Additional information about working for UNICEF can be found here. Advertised: 01 Oct 2026 W. Central Africa Standard Time Deadline: 08 Oct 2026 W. Central Africa Standard Time

At UNICEF, we are committed, passionate, and proud of what we do for as long as we are needed. Promoting the rights of every child is not just a job – it is a calling. UNICEF is a place where careers are built: we offer our staff diverse opportunities for professional and personal development that will help them reinforce a sense of purpose while serving children and communities across the world. We welcome everyone who wants to belong and grow in a diverse and passionate culture, coupled with an attractive compensation and benefits package. Visit our website to learn more about what we do at UNICEF. The Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) is responding to its 17th Ebola Virus Disease (EVD) outbreak, confirmed in May 2026 and affecting Ituri, North Kivu, and South Kivu provinces. The situation remains complex and evolving, with transmission occurring in both community and health-care settings. Response efforts are led by national authorities in a context shaped by health system limitations, logistical constraints, insecurity, displacement, and diverse community perceptions influencing health-seeking behaviors.UNICEF supports the Government through a multi-sectoral approach, focusing on community engagement, surveillance, infection prevention, and the continuity of essential services for vulnerable populations.This context requires strong coordination, adaptability, and cultural sensitivity to support effective and equitable response efforts, particularly for children and at-risk communities. Under the general guidance of the SBC/RCCE Specialist P3 and the direct supervision of the RCCE coordinator P4, the RCCE/Social and the Social & Behaviour Change Officer supports the design, implementation, monitoring, and reporting of evidence-based RCCE and SBC interventions for the Ebola response in Ituri, Noth Kivu, Tshopo, Bas Uele, Haut Uele and Bunia. The Officer contributes to community engagement, social listening, community feedback mechanisms, partner coordination, and capacity building to promote protective behaviours, strengthen community trust, and support timely, locally adapted response actions in affected and at-risk areas. Knowledge of a local language relevant to the duty station is considered an asset. Experience working with government counterparts, local authorities, community structures, UN agencies, coordination mechanisms, and implementing partners in insecure or hard-to-reach areas is considered an asset. Relevant experience at country level, particularly in development, fragile settings and humanitarian contexts. Relevant experience in a UN system agency or organization is considered an asset. As per Article 101, paragraph 3, of the Charter of the United Nations, the paramount consideration in the employment of the staff is the necessity of securing the highest standards of efficiency, competence, and integrity. This position has been assessed as an elevated risk role for Child Safeguarding purposes as it is either a role with direct contact with children, a role that works directly with identifiable children’s data, a safeguarding response role, or an assessed risk role. Additional vetting and assessment for elevated risk roles in child safeguarding (potentially including additional criminal background checks) apply. UNICEF is committed to fostering an inclusive, representative, and welcoming workforce. For this position, eligible and suitable female candidates are encouraged to apply. Government employees who are considered for employment with UNICEF are normally required to resign from their government positions before taking up an assignment with UNICEF. UNICEF does not charge a processing fee at any stage of its recruitment, selection, and hiring processes (i.e., application stage, interview stage, validation stage, or appointment and training). UNICEF will not ask for applicants' bank account information. UNICEF staff members holding fixed-term, continuing, or permanent appointments who are considered to be on abolished post status may apply for this temporary position and, if selected with a start date before 31 December 2025, may take it up as a temporary assignment, in line with UNICEF guidance on separation due to the abolition of posts or staff reduction. They will retain their fixed-term entitlements but will not hold a lien to their abolished post. For other scenarios where a Temporary Assignment may be possible, please refer to Additional guidance on IP to IP temporary assignments after completion of the full TOD.pdf (accessible to UNICEF personnel only). The conditions of a temporary assignment, including relocation entitlements, will depend on the status of the staff member's original appointment and may be limited in accordance with applicable UNICEF policies, procedures, and practices in force. Mobility is a condition of international professional employment with UNICEF and an underlying premise of the international civil service. Humanitarian action is a cross-cutting priority within UNICEF's Strategic Plan. UNICEF is committed to stay and deliver in humanitarian contexts. Therefore, all staff, at all levels across all functional areas, can be called upon to be deployed to support humanitarian response, contributing to both strengthening resilience of communities and capacity of national authorities. Eligible staff members on fixed-term, continuing or permanent contracts applying to IP TA positions in a duty station designated as L2/L3, may be able to retain a lien and their fixed-term entitlements, subject to approval by their Head of Office. The conditions of the temporary assignment will vary depending on the status of their post and relocation entitlements may be limited as per the relevant policies. All UNICEF positions are advertised, and only shortlisted candidates will be contacted and advance to the next stage of the selection process. An internal candidate performing at the level of the post in the relevant functional area, or an internal/external candidate in the corresponding Talent Group, may be selected, if suitable for the post, without assessment of other candidates. Additional information about working for UNICEF can be found here. Advertised: 01 Oct 2026 W. Central Africa Standard Time Deadline: 08 Oct 2026 W. Central Africa Standard Time

articles.job_description: Apply now Job no: 596057 Contract type: Temporary Appointment Location: Democratic Republic of Congo Categories: WASH (Water, Sanitation and Hygiene) UNICEF works in over 190 countries and territories to save children's lives, defend their rights, and help them fulfill their potential, from early childhood through adolescence. At UNICEF, we are committed, passionate, and proud of what we do for as long as we are needed. Promoting the rights of every child is not just a job – it is a calling. UNICEF is a place where careers are built: we offer our staff diverse opportunities for professional and personal development that will help them reinforce a sense of purpose while serving children and communities across the world. We welcome everyone who wants to belong and grow in a diverse and passionate culture, coupled with an attractive compensation and benefits package. Visit our website to learn more about what we do at UNICEF. The Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) is responding to its 17th Ebola Virus Disease (EVD) outbreak, confirmed in May 2026 and affecting Ituri, North Kivu, and South Kivu provinces. The situation remains complex and evolving, with transmission occurring in both community and health-care settings. Response efforts are led by national authorities in a context shaped by health system limitations, logistical constraints, insecurity, displacement, and diverse community perceptions influencing health-seeking behaviors.UNICEF supports the Government through a multi-sectoral approach, focusing on community engagement, surveillance, infection prevention, and the continuity of essential services for vulnerable populations.This context requires strong coordination, adaptability, and cultural sensitivity to support effective and equitable response efforts, particularly for children and at-risk communities. If you would like to know more about this position, please review the complete Job Description here: GVA - ToR WASH (IPC) Officer - NOB - Multiple DS.docx To qualify as a champion for every child you will have… Education: A university degree in Public Health, Environmental Health, Sanitary Engineering, or a related field is required. Work Experience: At least two (2) years of experience in relevant areas of water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH), water quality, public health, and environmental health. Previous experience in Ebola preparedness and response is mandatory. Knowledge of Infection Prevention and Control (IPC) protocols and guidelines, including those of the WHO and CDC. Willingness and availability to travel frequently throughout the Greater North Kivu Province. Skills: Strong teamwork skills and diplomatic ability. Ability to establish and maintain partnerships with government authorities and non-governmental organizations (NGOs). Innovative and resourceful mindset, with the ability to implement effective solutions in challenging environments. Ability to work under stressful conditions and demonstrate flexibility in carrying out responsibilities within a rapidly evolving operational context. Strong teamwork skills and diplomatic ability. Ability to establish and maintain partnerships with government authorities and non-governmental organizations (NGOs). Innovative and resourceful mindset, with the ability to implement effective solutions in challenging environments. Ability to work under stressful conditions and demonstrate flexibility in carrying out responsibilities within a rapidly evolving operational context. Language Requirements: Fluency in French is required. Language: Knowledge of another official UN language (Arabic, Chinese, Russian or Spanish) or a local language. Intermediate knowledge of English is considered an asset. IPC Protocols (WHO/CDC), Outbreak Control, Viral Hemorrhagic Fevers, Emergency Health Response, Field Mobility, Ebola Response Operations Relevant experience at country level, particularly in development, fragile settings and humanitarian contexts. Additional relevant postgraduate training that complements the primary degree will be considered a significant asset. Experience in the control of Ebola Virus Disease (EVD) outbreaks and/or other viral hemorrhagic fevers is highly desirable. Language: Knowledge of another official UN language (Arabic, Chinese, Russian or Spanish) or a local language. Intermediate knowledge of English is considered an asset. IPC Protocols (WHO/CDC), Outbreak Control, Viral Hemorrhagic Fevers, Emergency Health Response, Field Mobility, Ebola Response Operations Relevant experience at country level, particularly in development, fragile settings and humanitarian contexts. Additional relevant postgraduate training that complements the primary degree will be considered a significant asset. Experience in the control of Ebola Virus Disease (EVD) outbreaks and/or other viral hemorrhagic fevers is highly desirable. UNICEF's Core Values of Care, Respect, Integrity, Trust and Accountability and Sustainability (CRITAS) underpin everything we do and how we do it. Get acquainted with Our Values Charter: UNICEF Values UNICEF competencies required for this post are… (1) Builds and maintains partnerships (2) Demonstrates self-awareness and ethical awareness (3) Drive to achieve results for impact (4) Innovates and embraces change (5) Manages ambiguity and complexity (6) Thinks and acts strategically (7) Works collaboratively with others Familiarize yourself with our competency framework and its different levels. UNICEF promotes and advocates for the protection of the rights of every child, everywhere, in everything it does and is mandated to support the realization of the rights of every child, including those most disadvantaged, and our global workforce must reflect the diversity of those children. The UNICEF family is committed to include everyone, irrespective of their race/ethnicity, disability, gender identity, sexual orientation, religion, nationality, socio-economic background, minority, or any other status. UNICEF encourages applications from all qualified candidates, regardless of gender, nationality, religious or ethnic backgrounds, and from people with disabilities, including neurodivergence. We offer a wide range of benefits to our staff, including paid parental leave, breastfeeding breaks and reasonable accommodation for persons with disabilities. UNICEF provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process. If you require any accommodation, please submit your request through the accessibility email button on the UNICEF Careers webpage Accessibility | UNICEF. Should you be shortlisted, please get in touch with the recruiter directly to share further details, enabling us to make the necessary arrangements in advance. UNICEF does not hire candidates who are married to children (persons under 18). UNICEF has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the United Nations and UNICEF, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment, abuse of authority, discrimination, fraud, corruption and other forms of serious misconduct.UNICEF is committed to promoting the protection and safeguarding of all children. All selected candidates will undergo rigorous reference, safeguarding and background verification checks. These checks may include verification of academic credentials and employment history, screening against relevant United Nations misconduct databases, and requests for misconduct disclosures from current and former employers, professional associations, other relevant organizations and participating organizations under inter-agency safeguarding initiatives, including the Misconduct Disclosure Scheme (MDS), where applicable.Appointment, selection and continued engagement are subject to the satisfactory completion of all required checks. Selected candidates may be required to provide additional information and consent to enable UNICEF to undertake these checks.Background checks will include the verification of academic credential(s) and employment history. Selected candidates may be required to provide additional information to conduct a background check, and selected candidates with disabilities may be requested to submit supporting documentation in relation to their disability confidentially. UNICEF appointments are subject to medical clearance. Issuance of a visa by the host country of the duty station is required for IP positions and will be facilitated by UNICEF. Appointments are conditional on the selected candidates willingness to comply with current or future vaccination requirements, should UNICEF mandate it for personnel. Failure to comply with such requirements, where applicable and without a duly approved medical exemption from the relevant UN authority, will result in the cancellation of the selection or may lead to other administrative measures, including separation from service. As per Article 101, paragraph 3, of the Charter of the United Nations, the paramount consideration in the employment of the staff is the necessity of securing the highest standards of efficiency, competence, and integrity. This position has been assessed as an elevated risk role for Child Safeguarding purposes as it is either a role with direct contact with children, a role that works directly with identifiable children’s data, a safeguarding response role, or an assessed risk role. Additional vetting and assessment for elevated risk roles in child safeguarding (potentially including additional criminal background checks) apply. UNICEF is committed to fostering an inclusive, representative, and welcoming workforce. For this position, eligible and suitable female candidates are encouraged to apply. Government employees who are considered for employment with UNICEF are normally required to resign from their government positions before taking up an assignment with UNICEF. UNICEF reserves the right to withdraw an offer of appointment, without compensation, if a visa or medical clearance is not obtained, or necessary inoculation requirements are not met, within a reasonable period for any reason. UNICEF does not charge a processing fee at any stage of its recruitment, selection, and hiring processes (i.e., application stage, interview stage, validation stage, or appointment and training). UNICEF will not ask for applicants' bank account information. UNICEF staff members holding fixed-term, continuing, or permanent appointments who are considered to be on abolished post status may apply for this temporary position and, if selected with a start date before 31 December 2025, may take it up as a temporary assignment, in line with UNICEF guidance on separation due to the abolition of posts or staff reduction. They will retain their fixed-term entitlements but will not hold a lien to their abolished post. For other scenarios where a Temporary Assignment may be possible, please refer to Additional guidance on IP to IP temporary assignments after completion of the full TOD.pdf (accessible to UNICEF personnel only). The conditions of a temporary assignment, including relocation entitlements, will depend on the status of the staff member's original appointment and may be limited in accordance with applicable UNICEF policies, procedures, and practices in force. Mobility is a condition of international professional employment with UNICEF and an underlying premise of the international civil service. Humanitarian action is a cross-cutting priority within UNICEF's Strategic Plan. UNICEF is committed to stay and deliver in humanitarian contexts. Therefore, all staff, at all levels across all functional areas, can be called upon to be deployed to support humanitarian response, contributing to both strengthening resilience of communities and capacity of national authorities. Eligible staff members on fixed-term, continuing or permanent contracts applying to IP TA positions in a duty station designated as L2/L3, may be able to retain a lien and their fixed-term entitlements, subject to approval by their Head of Office. The conditions of the temporary assignment will vary depending on the status of their post and relocation entitlements may be limited as per the relevant policies. All UNICEF positions are advertised, and only shortlisted candidates will be contacted and advance to the next stage of the selection process. An internal candidate performing at the level of the post in the relevant functional area, or an internal/external candidate in the corresponding Talent Group, may be selected, if suitable for the post, without assessment of other candidates. Additional information about working for UNICEF can be found here. Advertised: 01 Oct 2026 W. Central Africa Standard Time Deadline: 08 Oct 2026 W. Central Africa Standard Time

articles.seo_description: فرصة عمل كمهندس بيانات (Data Engineer) لدى Orange Business بالجديدة بعقد دائم (CDI). مطلوب خبرة في هندسة البيانات وتقنيات البيانات الضخمة لتصميم وتطوير مسارات البيانات.
articles.final_html:
تعلن شركة Orange Business عن فتح باب الترشيح لشغل منصب مهندس بيانات (Data Engineer) بمدينة الجديدة، في إطار عقد عمل دائم (CDI).

المهام الرئيسية

  • تصميم وتطوير وصيانة مسارات البيانات القابلة للتوسع لدعم استراتيجية البيانات.

articles.job_description: Apporter l'appui à son entité dans le suivi des activités commerciales (ventes, recharges, animations) et participer au processus de contrôle de la qualité de service sur les aires de service. Au niveau de son périmètre géographique, l'Assistant Commercial est chargé de : Participer à la mise en place des actions d'animation commerciale (logistique, coordination terrain...) ; Assurer le suivi des ventes et recharges sur l'ensemble des canaux et participer au processus de gestion des stocks Jawaz et accessoires; Contribuer à la prospection commerciale en appui à l'agent commercial (préparation de fichiers, prise de contact, organisation de rendez-vous, suivi des leads...); Assurer le traitement administratif des opérations clients (suivi des alimentations, vérification règlements, préparation des éléments de facturation); Participer au traitement des demandes SAV (collecte des informations, préanalyse des dossiers, suivi jusqu'à clôture); Participer au contrôle de la qualité de service au niveau des points de vente et des aires de service selon le plan de contrôle mensuel; Contribuer à la collecte et à la mise à jour des données clients dans les systèmes (qualité, complétude, fiabilité); Veiller au respect des procédures et des standards d'ADM auprès du personnel des points de vente et auprès des partenaires au niveau des aires de service. NB: L'agent sera affecté à Marrakech dans le cadre de sa formation métier pour une période allant de 3 à 6 mois. Type d'horaire de travail : Normal, horaire administratif Être titulaire d'un diplôme de Technicien Spécialisé (Bac+2) en Commerce, Gestion des Entreprises, Marketing ou équivalent, promotion 2020, 2021, 2022, 2024, 2025 ou 2026. Connaissance des activités commerciales;

articles.job_description: Apply now Job no: 596036 Contract type: Fixed Term Appointment Duty Station: Damascus Location: Syrian Arab Republic Categories: WASH (Water, Sanitation and Hygiene) UNICEF works in over 190 countries and territories to save children’s lives, defend their rights, and help them fulfill their potential, from early childhood through adolescence. At UNICEF, we are committed, passionate, and proud of what we do for as long as we are needed. Promoting the rights of every child is not just a job – it is a calling. UNICEF is a place where careers are built: we offer our staff diverse opportunities for professional and personal development that will help them reinforce a sense of purpose while serving children and communities across the world. We welcome everyone who wants to belong and grow in a diverse and passionate culture, coupled with an attractive compensation and benefits package. Visit our website to learn more about what we do at UNICEF. UNICEF Syria Country Office works across all 14 governorates to advance the rights and well-being of children and women through humanitarian, early recovery and development programmes. It applies nexus and twin-track approaches to strengthen the transition towards more sustainable systems. Following the political transition in Syria in late 2024, the country is moving towards recovery and development; however, more than fourteen years of conflict, large-scale displacement, infrastructure damage, economic challenges and population returns continue to leave millions of people in need of essential services, including safe water, sanitation and hygiene services. UNICEF implements programmes through field offices and in partnership with government institutions, UN agencies, NGOs, academic institutions and community-based organizations to support the transition from humanitarian response to more resilient and sustainable service delivery systems. Within this context, the UNICEF Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) programme plays a critical role in ensuring equitable access to safe water, sanitation and hygiene services and promoting positive hygiene practices for vulnerable populations. UNICEF leads the WASH Sector in Syria and coordinates with national and sub-national partners to strengthen sector planning, information management, emergency preparedness and response. UNICEF WASH programmes support the rehabilitation and operation of water and sanitation infrastructure, climate-resilient and environmentally sustainable WASH interventions, capacity development of national institutions, and the delivery of life-saving services during humanitarian response. Through collaboration with government counterparts, water authorities, civil society organizations and humanitarian partners, UNICEF contributes to more sustainable WASH systems and improved public health outcomes for children and their communities across Syria. You can make a difference by bringing your WASH expertise, field experience and problem-solving skills to support quality, sustainable services for communities across southern Syria. In this role, you will help turn needs into practical WASH solutions, strengthen programme delivery and monitoring, work closely with partners and stakeholders, and adapt interventions to a dynamic operating environment—contributing directly to improved access to safe water, sanitation and hygiene for vulnerable communities. You will be based in the Damascus Field Office and cover five governorates: As-Sweida, Damascus, Dar’a, Quneitra and Rural Damascus. Communities in these areas face challenges related to access to essential services, damaged infrastructure, population movements and a dynamic operating environment shaped by evolving governance arrangements and security dynamics. You will report to the Chief of Field Operations and designated Officer-in-Charge and receive technical supervision from the Chief WASH. You will provide technical, operational and administrative support throughout the WASH programming cycle, including the development, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of WASH output results under the country programme and humanitarian response, with a geographic focus on the southern governorates. Summary of key functions/accountabilities: 2. Programme management, monitoring and delivery of results 3. Technical and operational support for programme implementation 4. Humanitarian WASH preparedness and response 6. Innovation, knowledge management and capacity building If you would like to know more about this position, please review the complete Job Description here: Classified Job Descriptions - WASH Officer (4).pdf To qualify as an advocate for every child you will have… Education : An adva nced university degree in one of the following fields is required: public health, social sciences, behavior change communication, sanitary engineering, environmental engineering, water resources engineering, water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) engineering or another relevant technical field. Work Experience : A minimum of two years of profe ssional work experience in WASH-related programmes in developing countries is required. At least one year of relevant experience in humanitarian response and/or early recovery is required. Skills : the ideal candidate should have strong skills in programme management, monitoring and evaluation, capacity building, AI tools, and Excel. Language Requirements : Fluency in Arabic and English is required. Language: Knowledge of another official UN language (Chinese, French, Russian or Spanish) is an asset. Desirable experience includes sector coordination, resource mobilization climate resilience and emergency preparedness. Experience in early recovery, as well as within the UN system, would be considered an asset. Relevant experience at country level, particularly in development, fragile settings and humanitarian contexts. UNICEF's Core Values of Care, Respect, Integrity, Trust and Accountability and Sustainability (CRITAS) underpin everything we do and how we do it. Get acquainted with Our Values Charter: UNICEF Values UNICEF competencies required for this post are… (1) Builds and maintains partnerships (2) Demonstrates self-awareness and ethical awareness (3) Drive to achieve results for impact (4) Innovates and embraces change (5) Manages ambiguity and complexity (6) Thinks and acts strategically (7) Works collaboratively with others (8) Nurtures, leads and manages people Familiarize yourself with our competency framework and its different levels. UNICEF promotes and advocates for the protection of the rights of every child, everywhere, in everything it does and is mandated to support the realization of the rights of every child, including those most disadvantaged, and our global workforce must reflect the diversity of those children. The UNICEF family is committed to include everyone, irrespective of their race/ethnicity, disability, gender identity, sexual orientation, religion, nationality, socio-economic background, minority, or any other status. UNICEF encourages applications from all qualified candidates, regardless of gender, nationality, religious or ethnic backgrounds, and from people with disabilities, including neurodivergence. We offer a wide range of benefits to our staff, including paid parental leave, breastfeeding breaks and reasonable accommodation for persons with disabilities. UNICEF provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process. If you require any accommodation, please submit your request through the accessibility email button on the UNICEF Careers webpage Accessibility | UNICEF. Should you be shortlisted, please get in touch with the recruiter directly to share further details, enabling us to make the necessary arrangements in advance. UNICEF does not hire candidates who are married to children (persons under 18). UNICEF has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the United Nations and UNICEF, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment, abuse of authority and discrimination based on gender, nationality, age, race, sexual orientation, religious or ethnic background or disabilities. UNICEF is committed to promote the protection and safeguarding of all children. All selected candidates will, therefore, undergo rigorous reference and background checks, and will be expected to adhere to these standards and principles. Background checks will include the verification of academic credential(s) and employment history. Selected candidates may be required to provide additional information to conduct a background check, and selected candidates with disabilities may be requested to submit supporting documentation in relation to their disability confidentially. UNICEF appointments are subject to medical clearance. Issuance of a visa by the host country of the duty station is required for IP positions and will be facilitated by UNICEF. Appointments are conditional on the selected candidates willingness to comply with current or future vaccination requirements, should UNICEF mandate it for personnel. Failure to comply with such requirements, where applicable and without a duly approved medical exemption from the relevant UN authority, will result in the cancellation of the selection or may lead to other administrative measures, including separation from service. As per Article 101, paragraph 3, of the Charter of the United Nations, the paramount consideration in the employment of the staff is the necessity of securing the highest standards of efficiency, competence, and integrity. UNICEF is committed to fostering an inclusive, representative, and welcoming workforce. For this position, eligible and suitable candidates are encouraged to apply. Government employees who are considered for employment with UNICEF are normally required to resign from their government positions before taking up an assignment with UNICEF. UNICEF reserves the right to withdraw an offer of appointment, without compensation, if a visa or medical clearance is not obtained, or necessary inoculation requirements are not met, within a reasonable period for any reason. UNICEF does not charge a processing fee at any stage of its recruitment, selection, and hiring processes (i.e., application stage, interview stage, validation stage, or appointment and training). UNICEF will not ask for applicants' bank account information. Humanitarian action is a cross-cutting priority within UNICEF's Strategic Plan. UNICEF is committed to stay and deliver in humanitarian contexts. Therefore, all staff, at all levels across all functional areas, can be called upon to be deployed to support humanitarian response, contributing to both strengthening resilience of communities and capacity of national authorities. Visa residence requirements: i.e. UNICEF shall not facilitate the issuance of a visa and working authorization for candidates under consideration for positions at the national officer and general service category. All UNICEF positions are advertised, and only shortlisted candidates will be contacted and advance to the next stage of the selection process. An internal candidate performing at the level of the post in the relevant functional area, or an internal/external candidate in the corresponding Talent Group, may be selected, if suitable for the post, without assessment of other candidates. Additional information about working for UNICEF can be found here. Advertised: 02 Oct 2026 Syria Standard Time Deadline: 09 Oct 2026 Syria Standard Time
